rounds.proof_sketch: With shape [16,256,256] and dim=1: inner_size=256, grid.y=(256+255)/256=1 (integer division), so inner_idx=blockIdx.y*256+threadIdx.x ranges [0,255]. The boundary inner_idx=256 is never reached. Original (>=256) and mutated (>256) both never trigger since max inner_idx=255.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the boundary check from inner_idx >= inner_size to inner_idx > inner_size, which would allow threads with inner_idx == inner_size to execute incorrectly. However, with the fixed input shape [16, 256, 256] and typical reduction dimension, inner_size equals 256 (for dim=1) or 65536 (for dim=0). Both values result in grid configurations where the maximum inner_idx exactly equals inner_size - 1, never reaching inner_size. The ceiling division formula for computing grid.y ensures no thread has inner_idx == inner_size when inner_size is a multiple of threads_per_block (256).
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under this fixed configuration. The mutation would be killable only if inner_size were NOT a multiple of 256 (threads_per_block), causing threads with inner_idx == inner_size to exist. With shape [16,256,256], all possible inner_size values (1, 256, 65536 depending on dim) result in exact grid sizing that prevents reaching the boundary.
rounds.recommendations: When mutation testing boundary conditions in GPU kernels, ensure test configurations include cases where the dimension sizes are NOT multiples of the thread block size, so boundary conditions are actually exercised. Here, using input shapes like [16, 257, 255] would expose the mutation.
